comparison: Both address AutoMitoC method validation (C1, C22-C24). OpenEval finds the method well-validated with strong evidence from qPCR correlation and comparisons. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the method is 'barely described' in the main manuscript and requesting more benchmarking and clarity about reproducibility.

Both evaluate AutoMitoC validation metrics (C25-C27, C74). OpenEval finds superior performance compared to previous methods as strong support. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the qPCR correlation is only 'moderate' and requesting more formal comparison with standard approaches using like-for-like samples.

Both address associations with age, sex, and ethnicity (C28-C32). OpenEval finds these demonstrate expected biological relationships serving as positive controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more thorough description and analysis of these factors, noting they are 'superficially described' and may confound downstream analyses.

Both evaluate blood cell count associations (C33-C36). OpenEval finds these appropriately quantified and supportive of method validity. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging these as known confounders that should be discussed in context without challenging the findings.

Both address GWAS results and quality control (C3, C37-C42). OpenEval finds comprehensive GWAS results with appropriate metrics as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 stating findings are 'convincing' and Reviewer 3 noting excellent reproducibility across studies.

Both evaluate enrichment of mtDNA depletion genes (C43-C45). OpenEval finds this provides biological validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers noting the enrichment is 'convincing' and shared across multiple studies, supporting reproducibility.

Both address comparisons with previous studies (C46-C49). OpenEval finds comparisons appropriately conducted though novelty claims are uncertain. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED but request more thorough contextualization, particularly with the Longchamps study, without challenging the replication statistics.

Both evaluate transethnic consistency (C50). OpenEval finds this further supports the findings. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 accepting the transethnic correlation but requesting more discussion of population structure confounding implications.

Both address lookup analyses and pathway enrichment (C51-C52 overlap with C53-C59). OpenEval finds mt-eQTL and heteroplasmy lookups provide functional context. Peer reviewers rate pathway findings as SUPPORTED, noting they 'argue convincingly' about cellular regulation, though requesting additional statistical tests comparing gene fractions.

Both evaluate pathway analysis and enrichment (C53-C59, C75-C76). OpenEval finds coherent pathway analysis with strong evidence for MT localization and specific pathways. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, stating findings are 'convincing' and show 'excellent reproducible science' across multiple studies.

Both address ExWAS results for SAMHD1 and TFAM (C4, C60-C64). OpenEval finds clear genome-wide significant findings with appropriately reported effect sizes. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, noting the rare variant analysis as an additional strength not found in other works, accepting the associations without critique.

Both evaluate phenome-wide associations with cancer (C5, C65-C67). OpenEval finds results with appropriate multiple testing correction and sensitivity analysis. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with both reviewers accepting the SAMHD1-cancer associations without expressing doubt.

Both address Mendelian randomization analysis for dementia (C6, C68-C71). OpenEval finds well-conducted MR with appropriate sensitivity tests, rating as SUPPORTED with appropriate qualifications. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether pleiotropy has been effectively ruled out and requesting additional heterogeneity tests and more detailed analyses.

Both evaluate overarching conclusions about biological processes and disease causality (C7-C8, C92-C94). OpenEval finds pathway conclusions well-supported but notes causal disease claims may be overstated. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, accepting biological interpretation but expressing doubt about causal disease relationships due to MR methodology concerns.

Partial overlap on conclusions about MT processes (C75-C76). OpenEval finds these well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating for broader conclusions (R13) reflects concerns about causal claims rather than the specific MT process findings.

Minimal overlap on method performance claims (C74). OpenEval finds superior concordance with WES provides quantitative support. Peer reviewers request more benchmarking but this specific comparison metric is not directly challenged.

OpenEval evaluates therapeutic speculation about SAMHD1 (C77-C78, C83-C84) as UNCERTAIN, noting it lacks direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific therapeutic claims.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C9-C21) as SUPPORTED, noting these are appropriately cited context-setting claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature summary on mtDNA-CN and dementia (C86-C88) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate contextualization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these literature summary claims.

OpenEval evaluates future speculation claim (C91) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is not a testable scientific claim but reasonable perspective. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this speculation.
